title: Polynomial-Time Choice-Word Verifier
statement: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and let $C,c$ be natural numbers. There is a language $V$ in polynomial time such that for every pair of binary strings $x,u$ with $|u|=C(|x|+1)^c$, the concatenation $xu$ belongs to $V$ if and only if the run of $N$ on input $x$ using choice word $u$ halts with output exactly $[1]$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
